CYCLEREVIEW_ICLR2025.argument: The paper studies the problem of Byzantine robust distributed learning and proposes an adaptive clipping scheme for the gradients before applying robust aggregation methods.
The paper theoretically shows that the proposed method preserves the robustness of the original aggregation method and empirically shows that it can improve the robustness of the learning.
The paper is well written and easy to follow.
The proposed method is simple and intuitive and the theoretical analysis is sound.
The experiments are well conducted and the results are promising.
The main weakness of the paper is that the theoretical analysis is not very strong.
The paper shows that the proposed method preserves the robustness of the original aggregation method, but it does not provide any new robustness guarantees.
The empirical results are promising, but it is not clear whether the proposed method is the best approach for Byzantine robust distributed learning.
